# Temple Scroll Column 17 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 17 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**17:1** He shall not acquire many wives for himself, lest they turn his heart away from Me.

**17:2** Nor shall he greatly increase silver and gold for himself.

**17:3** When he sits upon the throne of his kingdom, they shall write for him a copy of this law

**17:4** on a scroll, from that which is before the Levitical priests.

**17:5** It shall remain with him, and he shall read in it all the days of his life,

**17:6** that he may learn to fear Me and to keep all the words of this law

**17:7** and these statutes, by observing them.

**17:8** So that his heart may not be exalted above his brothers, and that he may not turn aside from the commandment, either to the right or to the left —

**17:9** so that he may prolong his days in his kingdom, he and his sons, in the midst of Israel.

**17:10** [vacat]

**17:11** You shall take the following for the ordination: one young bull and one ram from the flock,

**17:12** and unleavened bread, unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil —

**17:13** you shall make them of fine wheat flour.

**17:14** You shall place them in a single basket and present them in the basket,

**17:15** together with the bull and the two rams.

**17:16** You shall bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 17 is well preserved. The first section (lines 1-9) completes the Law of the King (cf. Deut 17:17-20), including prohibitions on accumulating wives, wealth, and the requirement to write and study a copy of the law. After a vacat section break, lines 11-16 begin the ordination instructions (millu'im), paralleling Exodus 29:1-4. The transition from constitutional law to priestly ordination is distinctive to the Temple Scroll's compositional logic.*
